identity.title: KVzip: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression with Context Reconstruction

problem.claim: Growing context lengths make KV-cache memory and attention latency costly during LLM inference.

gap.claim: Existing query-aware eviction methods reportedly degrade under multi-query use, even at a 90% cache-budget ratio.

contributions.claim: Introduces KVzip, a query-agnostic KV-cache eviction method designed to reuse compressed caches across diverse queries.
Ranks KV pairs by using the underlying LLM to reconstruct the original context, then evicts lower-importance pairs.
Reports compression and latency gains with negligible task-performance loss across several model and task settings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish KVzip through query-agnostic cache reuse based on context reconstruction from cached KV pairs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report 3–4× KV-cache size reduction and approximately 2× lower FlashAttention decoding latency.
Authors report negligible performance loss on question answering, retrieval, reasoning, and code comprehension tasks.
Authors report evaluations on LLaMA3.1, Qwen2.5, and Gemma3, with contexts up to 170K tokens, and significant gains over query-aware methods in multi-query scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM inference caches context as KV pairs, but longer contexts increase memory overhead and attention latency.
KVzip enables query-agnostic compressed-cache reuse and scores KV-pair importance through context reconstruction.
The authors report substantial cache and latency reductions with negligible task-performance loss, including long-context and multi-query evaluations.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects the eviction criterion directly to reconstructing the original context, rather than only to a particular downstream query.

lessons.interpretation: A task-independent objective can make a compressed representation reusable across changing query distributions.
lessons.application: When proposing reusable compression, define importance through reconstruction of a shared underlying representation and evaluate reuse across query types.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when queries have sharply different task-specific information requirements or reconstruction is substantially more expensive than query-aware scoring.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify cache-budget settings, latency hardware or baselines, evaluation metrics, or the quantitative meaning of “negligible” performance loss.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or reconstruction overhead, limiting assessment of end-to-end trade-offs.
